l.i: Plebes attonita meum videte. Heu, cum Virginibus meis tenellis Nunc omnis procul exulat Iuuentus.
PRESSA quum tantis socios vocarem Cladibus, fregere fidem, nec vllum Anxiis vani auxilium tulerunt Rebus amici.
Quum fames cunctos truculenta passim Perderet cives, Procerum Senatus, Et Sacerdotum vagus vrbe tota Languit ordo.
Namque ieiuno stimulante ventre Quasiit frustra sibi quisque fruges, Quasiit vires releuare pauco Pane ruentes.
At Deus vitia[?] mala dura gentis Cerne, vt occulto fremitu gemiscat Languidum pectus, tremulosque fundant Viscera planctus.
Quòd tua spreui pia iussa legis Contumax, extra furit ense muros Hostis infesto, violenta clausa Mors furit urbe.
Quividet fletus, simul & querelas Audit infirmes, recreare moestam Negligit,

page.notes: Printed "vitla" in stanza 4 is most likely "vitia" with a worn letter; marked [?]. "Quasiit" (stanzas 3) is copied as the long s appears; the Latin would normally read "Quaesiit", so verify the spelling. "Quividet" and "infirmes" are copied as printed. The last line "Negligit," is set flush right and belongs to the final stanza. Faint show-through of the reverse page on the right margin is omitted.
